_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Malaysia covering Malay kingdoms (Langkasuka, Kedah tua), Srivijaya suzerainty, Malacca Sultanate (1400-1511, Islamic hub), Portuguese/Dutch/British colonialism, Straits Settlements, Federated/Unfederated Malay States, Japanese occupation, Malayan Emergency 1948-1960, independence 1957, formation of Malaysia 1963 (Sabah/Sarawak/Singapore), race riots 1969, New Economic Policy, Mahathir's modernisation, 1MDB scandal, and ethnic power-sharing.

religion.note: Islam is official religion; shariah law applies to Muslims in family/personal matters; sultans are constitutional heads of Islam in their states; Yang di-Pertuan Agong is head of Islam nationally; non-Muslim freedoms constitutionally protected but tensions over conversions/proselytisation

ethnic_groups.name: Bumiputera (sons of soil)
ethnic_groups.notes: Constitutional category including Malays (55%) + indigenous groups; affirmative action/NEP benefits

ethnic_groups.name: Malay
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant politically; Islam and Malay language constitutional markers; UMNO historically dominant party; sultans are ethnically Malay; 'Ketuanan Melayu' (Malay supremacy) ideology; NEP post-1969 riots

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous (Orang Asli, Dayak, Kadazan-Dusun, Iban, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Orang Asli in Peninsular (~200K); Dayak/Iban/Bidayuh in Sarawak (majority there); Kadazan-Dusun/Murut in Sabah; Animist/Christian; some marginalised; distinct from Malay but share bumiputera status

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese Malaysian
ethnic_groups.notes: Hokkien/Cantonese/Hakka/Teochew; tin mining/commerce; dominant in economy; Penang/Kuala Lumpur/Johor; MCA party historically; DAP opposition; May 13 riots 1969 trauma; tension over NEP; Buddhist/Christian/Taoist

ethnic_groups.name: Indian Malaysian
ethnic_groups.notes: Mostly Tamil; British-era plantation workers (rubber estates); MIC party; Hindu temples; urban working/middle class; smaller Telugu, Malayali, Punjabi Sikh communities

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Eurasian, Peranakan, Thai, Cham, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Peranakan/Baba-Nyonya (Chinese-Malay mixed); Eurasian Portuguese Malacca community; small Thai in northern states; Cham refugees from Vietnam

independence.from: United Kingdom (Malaya); Malaysia formed 1963-09-16 with Sabah/Sarawak/Singapore (Singapore left 1965)

country_profile.notes_unique: Only federal elective monarchy globally (9 sultans rotate as Yang di-Pertuan Agong every 5 years); Petronas Twin Towers were world's tallest 1998-2004; 1MDB scandal (Najib Razak, Jho Low); New Economic Policy (NEP) affirmative action for Malays; Proton (national car); palm oil major producer

trade.notes: Highly trade-dependent; semiconductor supply chain critical globally; Penang back-end testing hub; palm oil top 2 exporter; CPTPP and RCEP member.

infrastructure.notes: World-class infrastructure; KLIA hub; Port Klang/Tanjung Pelepas among busiest globally; East Coast Rail Link (ECRL, Chinese-funded); Penang transport master plan.

governance_indices.notes: Post-2018 political reform era; Anwar Ibrahim PM (2022); UMNO/BN long dominance ended; multi-coalition politics; bumiputera affirmative action policies; Sedition Act concerns.

geography.terrain: Coastal plains rising to hills and mountains; Peninsular (Titiwangsa Range) and East Malaysia (Borneo, Crocker Range)
geography.notes: Two distinct regions (Peninsular and Borneo) separated by South China Sea; Borneo rainforests among world's oldest; Spratly Islands disputed; Strait of Malacca strategic choke point.

economy_extended.notes: Diversified economy; semiconductor manufacturing hub (Penang 'Silicon Island'); palm oil world's 2nd producer; Petronas state oil company; Vision 2030 targeting high-income status.

health.notes: Dual public-private system; medical tourism destination; affordable quality care; high childhood stunting surprising for income level; growing diabetes/NCD burden.

food_agriculture.notes: World's 2nd largest palm oil producer; rubber significant; 60%+ rice self-sufficient; durian major export crop; Sarawak pepper famous; FELDA smallholder scheme legacy.

security_stability.notes: Broadly stable; Five Power Defence Arrangements; Lahad Datu (2013) Sulu intrusion; ESSCOM eastern Sabah security zone; SCS disputes with China.

environment_climate.notes: Palm oil deforestation major issue; Borneo biodiversity hotspot (orangutan, pygmy elephant); haze from Indonesian fires; coral triangle marine biodiversity; peat fires.

demographics_extended.notes: Multi-ethnic (Malay 69%, Chinese 23%, Indian 7%); bumiputera privileges contentious; indigenous peoples (Orang Asli, Dayak, Kadazan); multi-religious; brain drain of non-Malay professionals.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Upper-middle-income; major palm oil and electronics exporter; multi-ethnic federation; Petronas twin towers.

world_heritage_sites: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of Straits of Malacca
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: The Star, New Straits Times (English); Berita Harian (Malay); Sin Chew Daily (Chinese); RTM, TV3, Astro; social media dominant.
cultural_heritage.notes: Multi-ethnic (Malay, Chinese, Indian, indigenous); Malacca Straits history; Petronas symbolism; food culture one of world's richest.

energy.notes: Petronas (national oil company; Petronas Towers); major LNG exporter (Sarawak); Bakun Dam (Sarawak); transitioning to renewable energy target 31% by 2025.

human_rights_gender.notes: Bumiputera affirmative action policies; ethnic tensions; dual legal system (civil + Sharia for Muslims); migrant worker issues; Sedition Act.

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law; Islamic Sharia for Muslims (personal status and some criminal offences)
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Sharia courts for Muslims in personal status (13 states + federal territories); limited criminal jurisdiction (RUU355 debate)
legal_system.customary_law_role: Adat (customary law) in Sabah, Sarawak, and some peninsular states
legal_system.notes: Federal Court (apex); dual system – civil and Sharia; Bumiputera constitutional provisions; National Security Council Act; reformed under Reformasi.

tourism.notes: Major tourism destination; Malaysia Truly Asia branding; food tourism; tropical islands; Borneo wildlife; medical tourism growing.

transport.notes: KLIA major regional hub; AirAsia (low-cost carrier HQ); ECRL (East Coast Rail Link) under construction; Penang LRT planned.

current_leader.name: Anwar Ibrahim
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Pakatan Harapan coalition; reformist; imprisoned twice (sodomy charges seen as politically motivated); deputy PM under Mahathir (1993-1998); Asian financial crisis fallout; finally PM after decades

yang_di_pertuan_agong.name: Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar
yang_di_pertuan_agong.title: Yang di-Pertuan Agong (King)
yang_di_pertuan_agong.notes: Sultan of Johor; ceremonial/constitutional monarch; rotates every 5 years among 9 hereditary state rulers

former_leaders.name: Muhyiddin Yassin
former_leaders.notes: 'Sheraton Move' backdoor coalition; Perikatan Nasional; COVID-19 pandemic; controversial

former_leaders.name: Mahathir Mohamad
former_leaders.notes: Second premiership; world's oldest PM (92); Pakatan Harapan; coalition collapsed

former_leaders.name: Najib Razak
former_leaders.notes: UMNO/BN; 1MDB scandal ($4.5B embezzled); defeated 2018; convicted, imprisoned 2022 (12 years)

former_leaders.name: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi
former_leaders.notes: UMNO; 'Mr Clean'; relative liberal; 2008 election losses; pressured to resign

former_leaders.name: Mahathir Mohamad
former_leaders.notes: Longest-serving PM; 'Look East' policy; Vision 2020; Petronas Towers; Asian financial crisis; Anwar Ibrahim sacking 1998; authoritarian streak

former_leaders.name: Abdul Razak Hussein
former_leaders.notes: UMNO; New Economic Policy (NEP) post-1969 riots; 'Father of Development'; died in office

former_leaders.notes: First PM; 'Father of Independence'; Alliance Party; Malaysia formation 1963; May 13 riots 1969; resigned
